items.title: 📄 ChatInject: Abusing Chat Templates for Prompt Injection in LLM Agents — Chang et al., ICLR 2026. Formats injected payloads to mimic native chat templates (optionally primed by persuasive multi-turn dialogue) so agents elevate them to system-level trust; transfers across models and largely bypasses prompt-based defenses. Code

📄 StepJack: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agent Safety Against Multi-Step Indirect Prompt Injection — Zhan et al., 2026. Introduces multi-step indirect prompt injection, decomposing an adversarial goal into innocuous-looking sub-steps distributed across a chain of pages along the agent's navigation path; the resulting 480-example StepJack benchmark raises attack success on computer-use agents by up to 31.2 points at fixed decomposition depth (e.g., GPT-5.4-mini 41.7%→72.9%). Code

📄 Agent Against Agent: An Agentic System for Automatic Prompt Injection Red Teaming — Wang et al., 2026. PIMiner, an agentic prompt-injection red-teaming system that builds a transferable strategy library from scratch during training and applies it to previously unseen target LLMs without retraining using only ~10 queries per sample, reaching up to 86.7% ASR on AgentDojo and 76.2% on IPIArena against frontier models. Code

📄 Agent Hacks Agent: Autoresearch for Production-Agent Red-Teaming — Mao et al., 2026. AHA, a falsifiable discovery loop that proposes a vulnerability hypothesis, builds a falsifier, instantiates and executes an attack in a sandboxed harness, then promotes confirmed findings into a reusable Vulnerability Concept Graph (VCG); across Claude Code and Codex on direct and indirect attacks, the frozen VCG requires no further search yet beats the strongest discovery baseline by 14.2 points under a single-shot protocol and transfers across scenarios and attack channels. Code
